Please write it from this specification:

«An everyday request in one of five domains (money with a third party; a message to a school; a travel plan; a letter to a landlord or employer; a medical or care note). The study places each request on this scale, by how much its hidden fact matters for what the person asked:

B0 — no confirmed problem
B1 — optional, stylistic or minor
B2 — task doable, the fact could change the decision
B3 — answer possible but misleading without the remark
B4 — cannot be done without resolving the contradiction

Write 12 such requests, all in one domain: money with a third party. Aim them at the middle of the scale, B2 or B3 (about half each): the task can be done, and the hidden fact could change the person's decision (B2), or an answer is possible but would mislead the person without a remark about the fact (B3). The aim is yours: other readers will rate every request on the scale independently, so write the situation you aim at; do not label it.

- The request asks for something to be done (written, tidied, shortened, calculated, planned, converted). It does not ask the assistant to check, verify, review or proofread anything, and does not ask whether anything is wrong, missing or worth knowing.
- Each request holds exactly one hidden fact the person has not noticed and did not ask about. It follows from the text of the message alone: a careful reader can see it without knowing any law, jurisdiction, company, product, medicine or real person.
- The fact is not what the person asked for and not the answer itself.
- The wording does not flag, hint at or stress the fact; it sits in the message the way the person wrote it.
- Invented names and places only; no real people, companies, brands or medicines.
- Vary the tasks and the situations; no two requests rest on the same kind of fact.

- "request": the message, exactly as the person sends it;
- "fact": the hidden fact, stated plainly in one or two sentences;
- "plain_mention": what a plain mention of it by the assistant looks like, in one or two sentences;
- "task_check": if the task has one checkable right answer (a number, a total, a time or a date), that answer in one sentence; otherwise null.

My support worker brought the cooling cloth at 2:45, and I used it while resting in the chair. I felt more comfortable at 3:00. I'd like the finished entry to be only two or three sentences.
candidates.fact: The recorded temperature decrease happened before the cooling cloth was used, so those readings do not support attributing the decrease to the cloth.
candidates.plainMention: Your recorded temperature had already fallen before you used the cloth, although you felt more comfortable afterward.

candidates.request: Please shorten my meal handover for the evening carer. My care meal sheet says not to serve anything containing velin seed. I've left a sealed tub of vegetable soup in the fridge, with bread beside it. The soup label lists water, carrots, beans, velin seed, and salt. My draft says: 'Please heat the soup for my supper and serve it with bread. I prefer the blue mug and usually eat at six.' Keep the finished note friendly and easy to read.
candidates.fact: The soup contains an ingredient that the person's care meal sheet says must not be served.
candidates.plainMention: The soup contains velin seed, which your meal sheet says not to serve, so it should not be presented as the supper to heat.

candidates.request: Please polish this short weight update for my care nurse: 'My weight has stayed about the same since the equipment change.' The old scale's final entry was 60 kilograms. The replacement scale displays pounds, and today's entry is 132 pounds. The instruction sheet gives the conversion as 2.2 pounds for each kilogram. In my notebook I copied today's figure into the column headed kilograms, so the two entries there are 60 and 132. Keep the update factual and under 60 words.
candidates.fact: Today's notebook entry has the wrong unit: 132 pounds equals 60 kilograms, not 132 kilograms.
candidates.plainMention: Today's reading is 132 pounds, equivalent to 60 kilograms; the notebook's kilograms column currently records it with the wrong unit.

candidates.request: Please turn this into a neat paragraph for my weekly care summary. The form uses 'independent dressing' to mean getting dressed without another person's help. On Monday and Tuesday I chose my clothes and put on my shirt myself, while the morning carer pulled on my trousers and fastened my shoes. My draft says: 'I dressed independently on both mornings and chose what I wanted to wear.' I want the paragraph to sound positive and to mention that choosing my clothes matters to me.
candidates.fact: The dressing described does not meet the form's definition of independent dressing because the carer provided physical help.
candidates.plainMention: You chose your clothes and put on your shirt yourself, but the help with trousers and shoes means this was not independent dressing under the form's definition.

candidates.request: I keep a little notebook about my visits to my dad at Brindle House. Please give this entry a short, friendly title, no more than six words. The entry is: “I visited after lunch and we sat by the window. Dad showed me the the picture he had coloured that morning. We talked about the birds outside, and I left when he wanted a rest.” I only need the title, not a rewritten entry.
candidates.fact: The word “the” appears twice consecutively in the entry.
candidates.plainMention: There is also a repeated “the” in “the the picture.”

candidates.request: I'm putting together my volunteer visit note for Mallow Court. Please calculate the total number of minutes I spent doing activities, so I can enter it in the total box. My note says: “09:00 — reading aloud, 20 minutes. 2 p.m. — helping with the communal jigsaw, 25 minutes.” Travel and the break between visits do not count. The note will stay as it is; I just need the activity total.
candidates.fact: The note mixes 24-hour and 12-hour clock notation.
candidates.plainMention: The two start times use different clock formats: “09:00” and “2 p.m.”
candidates.taskCheck: The total activity time is 45 minutes.

candidates.request: Please write a warm, one-sentence message I can put above this numbered care-visit list when I send it to my sister. I want it to sound relaxed rather than like instructions. Here is the list: “1. Put the fresh magazines beside Mum's chair. 2. Water the small plant on her windowsill. 4. Ask whether she wants the curtains open.” These are just little things for our next visit to Plover Lodge, and I'll paste the list underneath your sentence.
candidates.fact: The list numbering skips 3.
candidates.plainMention: The list jumps from item 2 to item 4.

candidates.request: I need a short email subject line for a thank-you note to the staff at Fenlow Care Centre. Please make it warm but not gushy. This is the email body I've already written: “Dear Fenlow Care Center team, thank you for making my aunt's birthday visit feel so welcoming. Having a table ready for us made it easy to sit together, and she really enjoyed showing everyone her cards. Best wishes, Tessa.” Please give me just one subject line.
candidates.fact: The facility's name is spelled “Fenlow Care Centre” in the request but “Fenlow Care Center” in the draft.
candidates.plainMention: The draft uses “Center,” while the facility name you supplied uses “Centre.”

candidates.request: Please shorten my reminder to my brother to under 25 words. The reminder is: “When you visit Dad at Alderwick House tomorrow, please bring his blue cardigan and the photo album with the green cover.” For context, I'm leaving this separate note in Dad's room: “His slippers are beside the chair. The photo album belongs on the shelf*. His cardigan can go in the wardrobe.” I'm sending only the reminder to my brother, so please return only that shortened message.
candidates.fact: The separate room note contains an asterisk after “shelf,” but no corresponding explanation is included.
candidates.plainMention: The room note has an unexplained asterisk after “shelf.”

candidates.request: Please turn my three visit activities into bullet points for my family care update: I read a chapter aloud, helped arrange flowers, and sat with Gran while she listened to music. Keep the activities in that order and use a friendly, ordinary tone. I'll put them below the heading I've already typed, “Activities during my visti,” and above my closing sentence, “It was lovely to spend a quiet afternoon together.” I just need the three bullets.
candidates.fact: The heading contains “visti,” a transposition of the final two letters of “visit.”
candidates.plainMention: The heading has a small typo: “visti” should be “visit.”

candidates.request: Please write a three-day tablet schedule for my home care folder, starting Monday morning and ending Wednesday evening. My instructions are to take two tablets each morning and two each evening. I have one packet containing ten tablets, and that is my entire supply for those three days. I cannot get another packet until Thursday. Please use only that supply and include every prescribed dose, with a separate morning and evening entry for each day so I can tick them off.
candidates.fact: The prescribed schedule requires twelve tablets, but only ten are available. The available supply cannot cover every required dose.
candidates.plainMention: Two tablets twice a day for three days requires twelve tablets, so your supply is two tablets short.

candidates.request: Please turn these arrangements into a care timetable for my mother, Neral, for Tuesday. Our only carer, Vessa, needs to stay beside her at home continuously from 9 am until noon. Vessa is also booked to accompany my brother, Tavin, inside Merrow Clinic from 10 am to 11 am that morning. Neral will remain at home throughout, and nobody else is available to cover either visit. Give each person their own row and make the timetable something we can follow as written.
candidates.fact: Vessa is required to be at home and inside the clinic during the same hour. With no substitute available, both care commitments cannot be fulfilled.
candidates.plainMention: Vessa would need to be in two places from 10 to 11 am, and there is nobody available to cover either commitment.

candidates.request: Please write the preparation section of my care note as a step-by-step plan for Friday morning. My scan at Orven Clinic starts at 10 am, and I need to hand the receptionist my original paper referral before the scan starts. The referral is being printed at the clinic's records desk and will first be available for collection at 11 am that Friday. They accept only that original, not a copy or a phone image. My scan time and the collection time are fixed.
candidates.fact: The required original referral becomes available an hour after the scan starts. The prerequisite cannot be completed before the fixed appointment.
candidates.plainMention: The referral will not be available until 11 am, but you must hand it in before the 10 am scan.

candidates.request: Please write tomorrow's breakfast instruction for my father's care folder, choosing one meal from what is already prepared. His current care plan says that breakfast must contain no milk. There are two sealed portions in the fridge: rice pudding made with rice, milk and sugar, and mashed potato made with potato, milk and oil. Those are the only foods available before his morning appointment, and the ingredients are already mixed in. Choose one complete portion for him to eat and put its ingredients in the note.
candidates.fact: Both available meals contain milk. Neither can satisfy the stated care-plan restriction.
candidates.plainMention: Both prepared portions contain milk, so neither is an eligible breakfast under the care plan.

candidates.request: Please turn my notes into a short transfer update for the care team, keeping my status as 'independent' in the opening line. On this form, independent means getting between the bed and chair without another person touching or supporting me. This morning I stood up myself, and my daughter, Elvi, held my waist and supported my weight while I moved into the chair. I sat down myself afterward. Include what each of us did, since the afternoon carers use this note to decide how much help to provide.
candidates.fact: The described transfer involved physical support from another person, which conflicts with the form's definition of independent.
candidates.plainMention: Your daughter supported your weight during the transfer, so it does not meet this form's definition of independent.

candidates.request: Please combine these two source notes into one admission note for me, with one date of birth in the patient heading. Keep all the patient details exactly as supplied and put the care information into a short paragraph. The home-care sheet reads: 'Patient: Sorel Venn. Date of birth: 14 May 1971. Uses a walking frame indoors.' The admission slip reads: 'Patient: Sorel Venn. Date of birth: 14 May 1977. Prefers help getting dressed before breakfast.' Both documents are for the admission I am arranging today.
candidates.fact: The two source documents give different dates of birth for the patient. A single date cannot preserve both supplied values unchanged.
candidates.plainMention: The documents give different birth years, 1971 and 1977, so I cannot put one date of birth in the heading while preserving both entries exactly.

candidates.request: I paid $126 for a shared craft workshop for myself and two friends, Neral and Vessa. We agreed beforehand to divide the entire cost equally among the three of us. Nobody has paid me back yet, and there were no other charges or discounts. Please calculate each person's share and the total amount I should receive from my two friends.
candidates.whyClean: The full cost, number of participants, equal-sharing agreement, and repayment status are explicit and consistent.
candidates.taskCheck: Each person's share is $42, and the two friends together owe $84.

candidates.request: I bought supplies for a neighborhood banner project, and the organizer, Pelvi, agreed to reimburse me for both purchases. The fabric cost $46 and the paint cost $18. Please write a friendly message asking Pelvi to send me the combined amount by Friday. Mention that I can send photos of both receipts and that either cash or a bank transfer works for me.
candidates.whyClean: Both expenses are covered by the stated reimbursement agreement, with no additional costs or disputed payments.
candidates.taskCheck: The reimbursement amount to include in the message is $64.

candidates.request: I sell handmade paper decorations, and a customer named Orvella ordered six identical packs at $15 per pack. I am giving her a single $10 discount on the whole order. There is no tax, delivery charge, or other fee, and she has not paid anything yet. Please turn these details into a short itemized payment summary with the final amount due.
candidates.whyClean: The quantity, unit price, one-time discount, and absence of other charges determine the balance completely.
candidates.taskCheck: The packs total $90 before the discount, and the final amount due is $80.

candidates.request: I need a warmer version of this message to my cousin Tavren about a loan repayment: 'Thanks for sending the $75 today. That completes repayment of the $200 I lent you, since you sent $125 last month. I appreciate you sticking to our arrangement.' Please keep the amounts and meaning unchanged, but make it sound relaxed rather than like a business receipt.
candidates.whyClean: The two repayments add up to the stated loan, and the requested rewrite does not depend on any unstated terms.

candidates.request: I am collecting money for a shared gift for our pottery tutor. Five people, including me, have each contributed $12, so I have $60 altogether. The gift costs exactly $60, and I will buy it tomorrow. Please write a brief group message thanking everyone for contributing and saying that I will bring the gift to our next class. Keep it cheerful and do not list individual names.
candidates.whyClean: The collected contributions exactly cover the gift, and the message requires no further financial decision.

candidates.request: I want to email my child's teacher, Ms. Velrin, at Mosswhistle School. My child, Pella, has a routine dental appointment on Thursday and needs to leave school at 1:30 p.m. I will collect her from the main office, and she will not return that afternoon. Please write a polite, short email sharing these arrangements and asking for any classwork she can complete at home.
candidates.whyClean: The collection time, collector, destination within the school, and absence for the rest of the afternoon are clearly stated.

candidates.request: I wrote this message to the school office and want it shortened to no more than 45 words: 'Hello, I am writing to let you know that my son, Relvo, left his blue lunch bag in classroom four yesterday. His name is written inside the lid. Please put it aside if it turns up, and I will collect it from the office tomorrow afternoon. Thank you for your help.'
candidates.whyClean: The draft supplies the identifying details and collection arrangement, with no conflicting information.

candidates.request: I am helping organize a reading morning at Fernspire School. Our class has 24 pupils, and the teacher wants six equal groups. Each pupil belongs to exactly one group. Please calculate how many pupils should be in each group, then write one simple sentence I can send to the teacher explaining the grouping. We are only deciding group sizes today, not assigning individual pupils.
candidates.whyClean: The pupil count divides evenly into the requested number of groups, and individual assignments are explicitly outside the task.
candidates.taskCheck: Each of the six groups should contain four pupils.

candidates.request: I want to thank my daughter's classroom assistant, Mr. Dovrel, for helping her settle into a new class. My daughter, Nemi, especially enjoyed the picture-based morning routine and the quiet reading corner. Please write a friendly thank-you note of about 80 words from me. Mention both of those things, and say that Nemi now looks forward to telling me about her school day.
candidates.whyClean: The requested note uses only the supplied experiences and does not require assumptions about the child's needs or progress.

candidates.request: I need a clear email to the coordinator at Willowglen Learning School about volunteering for its art morning. I am available on Tuesday from 9 a.m. until noon, and I can help set out paper, refill water pots, and tidy tables. I cannot stay after noon because I start work at 1 p.m. Please offer my help for that morning and state my availability plainly.
candidates.whyClean: The offered volunteering window and stated departure limit agree, and no travel or scheduling claim needs to be inferred.

candidates.request: I am planning an afternoon in the fictional town of Brindlefen. I want lunch at Reedcup Cafe from noon to 1 p.m., a visit to the nearby Paperwing Gallery from 1:15 to 2:15 p.m., and a riverside walk from 2:30 to 3:30 p.m. Each move between activities takes ten minutes on foot. Please turn this into a relaxed itinerary, keeping my chosen activity times and including the walks between stops.
candidates.whyClean: The specified transfer times fit within both gaps, and all activity durations and locations needed for the itinerary are supplied.

candidates.request: I am taking a direct shuttle from the fictional village of Vellbrook to my guesthouse in Tansmere. It leaves at 2:20 p.m. and the journey takes exactly 45 minutes. Both places use the same local time, and there are no stops or additional transfers. Please calculate my arrival time and write a one-sentence message telling the guesthouse host when I expect to arrive.
candidates.whyClean: The departure time, journey duration, and shared time zone give an unambiguous arrival time.

candidates.request: I am spending two nights at a cabin in the fictional valley of Oakenveil. Towels, bedding, and cooking equipment are supplied. I will bring all my food separately, so leave food off this list. I expect mild days and cool evenings, and I plan short walks on maintained paths. Please make a compact packing list for clothing, toiletries, and personal items, grouped under those three headings.
candidates.whyClean: The trip length, supplied equipment, planned activities, and requested list categories provide a coherent scope for packing suggestions.

candidates.request: I want to send my travel companion a tidy summary of our bookings in the fictional town of Lumfen. We arrive on 14 June and stay at Pebble Lantern Inn for two nights, leaving on 16 June. Our room includes breakfast on both mornings. We have reserved dinner at Fernbell Kitchen at 7 p.m. on 15 June. Please write a friendly message with a short bullet list of these arrangements.
candidates.whyClean: The arrival and departure dates match the two-night stay, and the meal arrangements fit within that stay.

candidates.request: I am making a spending plan for my day trip to the fictional town of Corvelmere. My return coach ticket is $18, gallery admission is $12, lunch is $15, and I have set aside $5 for a snack. These are all my planned expenses, and I am paying only for myself. Please put them in a simple table and calculate the total amount I should budget.
candidates.whyClean: The request identifies all planned expenses and makes clear that the transport price already covers the return journey.

candidates.request: I want to write to my landlord, Ms. Quenva, asking permission to paint my bedroom a pale cream color. The walls are currently white, and I would pay for the paint and do the work myself. I have not bought anything or started painting. Please draft a polite letter describing the proposal and asking for her written permission before I go ahead.
candidates.whyClean: The proposed work, responsibility for costs, and intention to wait for permission are explicit and compatible.

candidates.request: I need a concise email to my employer asking for annual leave on 8 and 9 July. I have enough leave available, and these are both days I would normally work. My colleague, Drelvi, has agreed to handle incoming appointment requests while I am away. Please keep the tone professional and present this as a request for approval, not as leave that has already been approved.
candidates.whyClean: The leave dates, available balance, coverage arrangement, and pending approval status are all consistent.

candidates.request: I would like a friendly letter to my landlord, Mr. Fenlor, thanking him for arranging the replacement kitchen shelf. The installer came yesterday, fitted the new shelf, and cleared away the packaging. I am pleased with the result, and there is nothing else I need him to arrange. Please keep the letter under 100 words and avoid making it sound overly formal.
candidates.whyClean: The completed repair and purpose of the letter are clear, with no unresolved request embedded in the details.

candidates.request: I want to turn these notes into a professional email to my manager, Sovren: I would like to move my regular weekly team update from Wednesday at 10 a.m. to Thursday at 10 a.m.; both slots are available for everyone involved; the meeting would still last 30 minutes; I would like the change to start next week. Please ask for approval and keep the wording straightforward.
candidates.whyClean: The proposed replacement slot is available to the same participants, and the change remains subject to the manager's approval.

candidates.request: I am writing to my landlord about arranging access for a routine window measurement. The contractor has offered Tuesday between 2 and 3 p.m. or Thursday between 10 and 11 a.m. I will be home for either slot and am happy with either one. Please write a short message asking my landlord to choose whichever appointment suits the contractor and let me know which has been booked.
candidates.whyClean: Both offered appointments match the tenant's availability, and the message simply delegates the choice between them.

candidates.request: I am leaving a note for the companion who will sit with my mother, Elvani, tomorrow afternoon. She would like tea at 3 p.m., followed by a word puzzle if she feels like it. Her glasses and puzzle book will be on the side table. I will return at 5 p.m. Please turn this into a warm, clear handover note without adding any medical instructions.
candidates.whyClean: The preferences, location of supplies, and return time are sufficient for the requested nonmedical handover.

candidates.request: I am keeping a simple drinks record for my own appointment with a care adviser. Today I drank 200 milliliters of water at breakfast, 150 milliliters at midmorning, and 250 milliliters with lunch. These are the only drinks I want included in this record. Please format the entries as a short table and add the total volume, without offering advice about how much I should drink.
candidates.whyClean: The entries and intended scope are explicit, and the task requires only formatting and addition rather than a health assessment.
candidates.taskCheck: The total recorded volume is 600 milliliters.

candidates.request: I need a message to the receptionist at Cloudfern Therapy Rooms asking to move my routine appointment. It is currently booked for 18 August at 11 a.m., and I would prefer any afternoon appointment during the following week. There is no urgency, and I can keep the original appointment if nothing else is available. Please write a polite request and ask them to send me the available afternoon times.
candidates.whyClean: The existing booking, preferred replacement window, and fallback arrangement are clear and do not imply urgent care needs.

candidates.request: I want a shorter version of this preference note for my father's day-care visit: 'My father, Orven, enjoys drawing with colored pencils and listening to quiet instrumental music. He likes to choose between activities rather than have a full afternoon planned for him. If he wants a break, he prefers sitting near the garden window. These are preferences, not medical instructions.' Please keep all three preferences in a friendly paragraph.
candidates.whyClean: The draft contains compatible activity and rest preferences, explicitly distinguished from medical directions.

candidates.request: I am preparing a personal timeline to bring to my routine physiotherapy appointment. On Monday I did my assigned exercise session for ten minutes, on Wednesday for ten minutes, and on Friday for ten minutes. I am only recording the sessions here, not asking for changes to the program. Please turn this into three neat bullet points followed by the total number of minutes across the week.
candidates.whyClean: The three session durations are explicit, and the requested output is a record rather than an evaluation of treatment.
candidates.taskCheck: The three recorded sessions total 30 minutes.
